awards.title: Hack The North 2024 FINALIST
awards.description: On September 15th, I won the finalist award at Hack The North. My team built a robotic arm that detects muscle signals using ECG sensors. When detected, servos on the arm band assist in bending your fingers. There are also games you can play to keep you entertained as you work through your recovery!

awards.title: University of Windsor SSPC WINNER - 2023
awards.description: On December 8th, 2023, my team of three won first place at the Secondary School Programming Competition hosted at the University of Windsor. Each of us received a $3000 scholarship for a program at the university, along with a monetary prize. I teamed up with Gurjas Dhillon and Dorothy Zheng, all of us from Vincent Massey Secondary School. This event was a time to remember, and I had a lot of fun

posts.text: I'm thrilled to announce my win at NexHacks, where our team won the Deepest Researched Chain prize from Seda! 🔥 Our team created GenZNews 📰, a project that aims to solve two problems simultaneously: 1. News you see on reels is often biased and untrustworthy. 2. Articles and videos from more reputable news sources can still feel a bit dry to consume, and lack some modern humour. With two clicks, you can deep research a genre of your choice (sports, politics, etc.) and generate a 3D visualization

Only two weeks late! 🔥 I'm proud to announce my win at Hack the North, Canada's Largest hackathon! 🍁 We won the Genesys prize from our project BeyondSight! BeyondSight is designed to help deafblind people with indoor navigation. It uses SLAM for localization, and YOLO to map out obstacles in 3D space. It also navigates you around obstacles with A*.
